chapter_title: The Chapter of the Four Kingdoms
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly a late homiletic/pastoral piece built around a Gospel saying (bread and water to a disciple) and applied to Manichaean community categories (catechumens, righteous/elect), with exhortation to almsgiving and promise of eschatological reward. It lacks the hallmark “cosmos→cosmos” systematic correspondential mappings (degrees, body–universe maps, cosmic mechanics). The opening is explicitly hagiographic frame (“the apostle speaks”), and the rest is an ethical application contrasting charity with the worldly “four kingdoms.”

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic/dialogue attribution (“Once again the apostle speaks”) marks the editorial frame; not part of the old impersonal cosmological substrate.

Worldly-geopolitical list (Babylon/Persia, Romans, Axumites, Silis) functions as rhetorical set-up for later moral exhortation; not a cosmic-degree mapping and not a frame formula, so best read as late homiletic/application material rather than core substrate.

Paraphrase of a Gospel-style saying (bread and cup of water given to a disciple “on account of the name of God”) with direct address (“I say to you in truth”) and moral comparison; the entry-vector is Christian/Gospel tradition rather than the pre-compilation cosmological system.
Institutional Manichaean categories and practice (“catechumen,” giving bread/water; promise of ‘rest for ever’) indicate church/community exhortation rather than cosmological exposition.
Explicit Gospel citation formula (“Just as the saying that the good saviour uttered…”) makes this a Christian overlay regardless of correspondential potential in the saying itself.

Interpretive gloss on the saviour’s words (“Now, the saviour is calling…”) and application to catechumens; this is Gospel-derived homily with institutional targets, not an internal cosmological mapping.

Community-identification teaching (“faithful catechumen,” “faithful righteous one”) with indwelling ‘Holy Spirit’ functions as ethical/institutional instruction; no cosmos→cosmos mechanics or degree-structure markers.
Almsgiving/fellowship instruction plus reward logic (“last day,” ‘give thanks before his true father’) is pastoral-eschatological application within the community rather than systematic cosmology.
Concluding exhortation/beatitude-style blessing (“Blessed are these… hear and believe…”) is application voice closure, not substrate exposition.
